sentences.zh: 25%租庸調之法，以人丁為本。

translations.literal: The law of zu, yong, and diao took registered males as its basis.
translations.idiomatic: The zu-yong-diao tax system was founded on the registered male population.

sentences.zh: 自開元以後，天下戶籍久不更造，丁口轉死，田畝賣易，貧富升降不實。

translations.literal: From after the Kaiyuan era onward, household registers throughout the realm were long left unrevised; as persons died or were transferred, fields were sold or exchanged, and the rise and fall of wealth and poverty were not truthfully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaiyuan period, national household registers went unrevised for years. Deaths and transfers went unrecorded, land changed hands, and the real distribution of wealth no longer matched the books.

sentences.zh: 其後國家侈費無節，而大盜起，兵興，財用益屈，而租庸調法弊壞。

translations.literal: Thereafter the state spent without restraint, great bandits arose, warfare flared, resources grew ever tighter, and the zu-yong-diao system broke down.
translations.idiomatic: State expenditure then ran without limit, major rebellions broke out, and war drained the treasury until the zu-yong-diao system collapsed.

sentences.zh: 自代宗時，始以畝定稅，而斂以夏秋。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Daizong, taxation began to be fixed by the mu, and collection was divided between summer and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daizong, taxes were first assessed by acre and collected in summer and autumn installments.

sentences.zh: 至德宗相楊炎，遂作兩稅法，夏輸無過六月，秋輸無過十一月。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong made Yang Yan his chief minister, the Two-Tax Law was instituted: summer payments were due no later than the sixth month, autumn payments no later than the eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong elevated Yang Yan to chief minister, he enacted the Two-Tax Law, setting a summer deadline in the sixth month and an autumn deadline in the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 置兩稅使以總之，量出制入。

translations.literal: Commissioners for the two taxes were appointed to oversee it; revenue was set by measuring outlays and fixing intake.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Two-Tax commissioners to administer the system, fixing revenue by estimating expenditures first.

sentences.zh: 戶無主、客，以居者為簿；

translations.literal: Households were no longer divided into resident and guest registers; those who dwelt in a place were entered on its rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Registers no longer distinguished "resident" from "guest" households; whoever actually lived in a district was recorded there.

sentences.zh: 人無丁、中，以貧富為差。

translations.literal: Persons were no longer classified as adult or youth; gradations were made according to wealth and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Adult and youth categories were dropped; liability was graded by wealth instead.

sentences.zh: 商賈稅三十之一，與居者均役。

translations.literal: Merchants were taxed one-thirtieth and shared corvée duties equally with residents.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants paid a thirty-to-one levy and bore corvée obligations on the same basis as residents.

sentences.zh: 田稅視大曆十四年墾田之數為定。

translations.literal: Field tax was fixed according to the number of cultivated mu recorded in the fourteenth year of the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax was pegged to the acreage under cultivation as recorded in Dali year 14.

sentences.zh: 遣黜陟使按比諸道丁產等級，免鰥寡惸獨不濟者。

translations.literal: Inspection commissioners were sent to compare household registers and grade productive capacity in each circuit, exempting widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute who could not pay.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched inspection commissioners to verify registers, rank productive capacity by circuit, and exempt widowers, widows, orphans, and others too poor to pay.

sentences.zh: 敢有加斂，以枉法論。

translations.literal: Anyone who added extra levies was to be punished under the statute on perversion of law.
translations.idiomatic: Any official who imposed surcharges was liable for prosecution as a law-breaker.

sentences.zh: 議者以租、庸、調，高祖、太宗之法也，不可輕改。

translations.literal: Critics held that zu, yong, and diao were the laws of Gaozu and Taizong and ought not be lightly altered.
translations.idiomatic: Opponents argued that zu, yong, and diao were the fiscal foundations laid by Gaozu and Taizong and must not be lightly discarded.

sentences.zh: 而德宗方信用炎，不疑也。

translations.literal: But Dezong was then placing full trust in Yan and had no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, however, was wholly convinced by Yang Yan and would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 舊戶三百八十萬五千，使者按比得主戶三百八十萬，客戶三十萬。

translations.literal: Former households numbered 3,805,000; after the commissioners compared registers, resident households came to 3,800,000 and guest households to 300,000.
translations.idiomatic: The old registers listed 3,805,000 households; after review, resident households totaled 3,800,000 and guest households 300,000.

sentences.zh: 天下之民，不土斷而地著，不更版籍而得其虛實。

translations.literal: The people of the realm were bound to the land without territorial reassignment, and the true state of affairs was obtained without revising the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: The people were tied to where they actually lived without redrawing territorial boundaries, and the government learned the real situation without overhauling the registers.

sentences.zh: 歲斂錢二千五十餘萬緡，米四百萬斛，以供外；

translations.literal: Each year there were collected more than 20,500,000 strings of cash and 4,000,000 bushels of grain for external supply.
translations.idiomatic: Annual collections yielded more than 20.5 million strings of cash and four million bushels of grain for provincial circuits.

sentences.zh: 錢九百五十餘萬緡，米千六百餘萬斛，以供京師。

translations.literal: More than 9,500,000 strings of cash and more than 16,000,000 bushels of grain were supplied to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The capital received more than 9.5 million strings of cash and over sixteen million bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 稅法既行，民力未及寬，而朱滔、王武俊、田悅合從而叛，用益不給，而借商之令出。

translations.literal: The tax law had only just been put in force and the people's strength had not yet been eased when Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, and Tian Yue joined in rebellion; expenditures grew insufficient and the order to borrow from merchants was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The new tax law had barely taken effect and the people had not yet felt relief when Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, and Tian Yue rebelled together. Revenue fell short, and the court ordered loans from merchants.

sentences.zh: 初，太常博士韋都賓、陳京請借富商錢，德宗以問度支杜佑，以為軍費裁支數月，幸得商錢五百萬緡，可支半歲。

translations.literal: At first the Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Wei Dubin and Chen Jing requested borrowing money from wealthy merchants; Dezong asked the Director of Revenue Du You, who held that military expenses would barely last a few months and that if merchant funds of five million strings could be obtained, they would suffice for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Wei Dubin and Chen Jing first proposed borrowing from rich merchants. Dezong consulted Du You, director of revenue, who replied that army funds would last only a few months but that five million strings from merchants could sustain the war for half a year.

sentences.zh: 乃以戶部侍郎趙贊判度支，代佑行借錢令，約罷兵乃償之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan was put in charge of the Directorate of Revenue to replace You and carry out the borrowing order, with repayment promised once the troops were disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan, vice minister of revenue, was assigned to the directorate of revenue to replace Du You and enforce the loan order, with repayment promised after the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 京兆少尹韋楨、長安丞薛萃，搜督甚峻，民有不勝其冤自經者，家若被盜。

translations.literal: The Vice Prefect of Jingzhao Wei Zhen and the Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an Xue Cui pressed the search and collection with extreme severity; some people, unable to bear the injustice, hanged themselves, and households were ravaged as if by robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen, vice prefect of Jingzhao, and Xue Cui, assistant magistrate of Chang'an, enforced collection with brutal severity. Some victims hanged themselves in despair; households were stripped as if by bandits.

sentences.zh: 然總京師豪人田宅、奴婢之估，裁得八十萬緡。

translations.literal: Yet in totaling the assessed value of estates, slaves, and servants of the wealthy in the capital, only eight hundred thousand strings were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet valuing the mansions, land, and slaves of the capital's rich produced only eight hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 又取僦櫃納質錢及粟麥糶於巿者，四取其一，長安為罷市，市民相率遮邀宰相哭訴，盧杞疾驅而過。

translations.literal: They also took one-fourth from pawn deposits and from grain and wheat sold in the market; Chang'an markets shut down, and townspeople in groups blocked and wept before the chief minister as he passed; Lu Qi whipped his carriage on through.
translations.idiomatic: They also levied one quarter on pawn deposits and on grain sold in the markets. Chang'an shut its markets; crowds blocked the chief minister's path, weeping in protest, while Lu Qi drove past without stopping.

sentences.zh: 韋楨懼，乃請錢不及百緡、粟麥不及五十斛者免，而所獲裁二百萬緡。

translations.literal: Wei Zhen, in fear, then requested exemption for sums under one hundred strings or grain and wheat under fifty bushels, yet what was obtained amounted to only two million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing riot, Wei Zhen secured exemption for sums under one hundred strings or fifty bushels of grain, but the haul still reached only two million strings.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少游增其本道稅錢，每緡二百，因詔天下皆增之。

translations.literal: The military governor of Huainan, Chen Shaoyou, increased tax money in his circuit to two hundred cash per string, and an edict followed ordering the increase throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou, military governor of Huainan, raised his circuit's tax assessment to two hundred cash per nominal string, and an edict extended the increase empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 自太宗時置義倉及常平倉以備凶荒，高宗以後，稍假義倉以給他費，至神龍中略盡。

translations.literal: From Taizong's time charity granaries and ever-normal granaries were established to guard against famine; after Gaozong they were gradually lent for other expenses, and by the Shenlong era they were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had established charity granaries and ever-normal granaries against famine. After Gaozong they were repeatedly diverted to other expenses, and by the Shenlong era the reserves were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，復置之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong restored them on his accession.

sentences.zh: 其後第五琦請天下常平倉皆置庫，以畜本錢。

translations.literal: Later Diwu Qi requested that every ever-normal granary in the realm have storehouses built to hold capital funds.
translations.idiomatic: Later Diwu Qi proposed that every ever-normal granary in the empire maintain storehouses holding operating capital.

sentences.zh: 至是趙贊又言：「自軍興，常平倉廢垂三十年，凶荒潰散，餧死相食，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: At this time Zhao Zan again said: "Since the outbreak of war the ever-normal granaries have lain abandoned for nearly thirty years; amid famine people scattered and starved, feeding on one another in numbers beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan now argued: "Since the wars began, ever-normal granaries have been neglected for nearly thirty years. Famine drove people apart; they starved in such numbers that corpses fed the living beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，京城兩市置常平官，雖頻年少雨，米不騰貴，可推而廣之，宜兼儲布帛。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers have been placed in the two markets of the capital; though rain was scant in successive years, grain did not soar in price. This may be extended broadly; cloth and silk should also be stored.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers in the capital's two markets have kept grain prices steady despite poor rains. The system should be expanded, and cloth and silk stockpiled as well.

sentences.zh: 請於兩都、江陵、成都、揚、汴、蘇、洪置常平輕重本錢，上至百萬緡，下至十萬，積米、粟、布、帛、絲、麻，貴則下價而出之，賤則加估而收之。

translations.literal: He requested that in the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yang, Bian, Su, and Hong, ever-normal capital be set in light and heavy amounts from one million strings down to one hundred thousand, storing rice, millet, cloth, silk, thread, and hemp; when prices were high they would sell at reduced price, when low they would buy at added valuation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ever-normal funds from one million strings down to one hundred thousand at the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Bian, Suzhou, and Hongzhou, stockpiling grain, cloth, silk, and hemp to sell cheap when prices rose and buy dear when they fell.

sentences.zh: 諸道津會置吏，閱商賈錢，每緡稅二十，竹、木、茶、漆稅十之一，以贍常平本錢。

translations.literal: At ferry crossings in each circuit officers were to be placed to inspect merchants' cash, taxing twenty cash per string, and bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer one-tenth, to support ever-normal capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tax agents at circuit crossings were to inspect merchant funds, levy twenty cash per string, and take one-tenth on bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer to fund the ever-normal reserves.

sentences.zh: 」德宗納其策。

translations.literal: " Dezong adopted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 屬軍用迫蹵，亦隨而耗竭，不能備常平之積。

translations.literal: But as military needs pressed urgently, the stores were consumed in turn and could not maintain ever-normal accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: Military demand soon consumed the reserves, and ever-normal stockpiles could not be maintained.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道討賊，兵在外者，度支給出界糧。

translations.literal: At this time, in the various circuits' campaigns against rebels, troops abroad were supplied with grain from beyond their borders by the Directorate of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: While circuits campaigned against rebels, the directorate of revenue supplied grain to armies operating outside their home territories.

sentences.zh: 每軍以臺省官一人為糧料使，主供億。

translations.literal: Each army had one official from the central ministries as grain commissioner, in charge of provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: Each army appointed one capital official as grain commissioner to manage supplies.

sentences.zh: 士卒出境，則給酒肉。

translations.literal: When soldiers crossed the border, wine and meat were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers received wine and meat once they crossed a border.

sentences.zh: 一卒出境，兼三人之費。

translations.literal: One soldier crossing the border entailed the expense of three men.
translations.idiomatic: A single soldier abroad cost the treasury three men's rations.

sentences.zh: 將士利之，逾境而屯。

translations.literal: Officers and troops profited by this and encamped beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Officers profited from the arrangement and kept troops camped across borders.

sentences.zh: 趙贊復請稅間架，算除陌。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan again requested taxation on structures and calculation of the transaction-stamp levy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan next proposed the structure tax and the transaction-stamp levy.

sentences.zh: 其法：屋二架為間，上間錢二千，中間一千，下間五日；

translations.literal: The rule was: two roof-bays counted as one bay-unit; an upper bay two thousand cash, a middle bay one thousand, a lower bay five hundred cash;
translations.idiomatic: Two roof-bays formed one taxable unit: upper units at two thousand cash, middle at one thousand, lower at five hundred cash;

sentences.zh: 匿一間，杖六十，告者賞錢五萬。

translations.literal: concealing one bay-unit brought sixty blows of the staff, and informers were rewarded fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: concealing a unit brought sixty blows of the staff; informers received fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 除陌法：公私貿易，千錢舊算二十，加為五十；

translations.literal: The transaction-stamp rule: in public and private trade, twenty cash per thousand had been levied and this was raised to fifty;
translations.idiomatic: For the transaction-stamp levy on public and private trade, the old rate of twenty cash per thousand was raised to fifty;

sentences.zh: 物兩相易者，約直為率。

translations.literal: where goods were exchanged for goods, estimated value served as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: where goods were bartered, estimated value set the rate.

sentences.zh: 而民益愁怨。

translations.literal: The people grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Popular resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 及涇原兵反，大謼長安市中曰：「不奪爾商戶僦質，不稅爾間架、除陌矣。

translations.literal: When the Jingyuan troops rebelled, they shouted in the streets of Chang'an: "We will not seize your merchants' pawn deposits or tax your structure and stamp levies!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyuan troops mutinied, they shouted through Chang'an: "We will not seize your pawn deposits or tax your structure and stamp dues!"

sentences.zh: 」於是間架、除陌、竹、木、茶、漆、鐵之稅皆罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the structure tax, transaction-stamp levy, and taxes on bamboo, timber, tea, lacquer, and iron were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The structure tax, stamp levy, and taxes on bamboo, timber, tea, lacquer, and iron were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 朱泚平，天下戶口三耗其二。

translations.literal: After Zhu Ci was pacified, two-thirds of the realm's registered population had been lost.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's defeat, two-thirds of the empire's registered population was gone.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，詔天下兩稅審等第高下，三年一定戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, an edict ordered that throughout the realm the grades of the two taxes be reviewed for high and low, and households be fixed every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 an edict ordered circuits to review two-tax grades and fix household registers every three years.

sentences.zh: 自初定兩稅，貨重錢輕，乃計錢而輸綾絹。

translations.literal: From the first fixing of the two taxes, goods were heavy and cash light, so payment was calculated in cash but delivered in silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the two taxes were first fixed, commodities were costly and cash cheap, so assessments were reckoned in money but paid in silk.

sentences.zh: 既而物價愈下，所納愈多，絹匹為錢三千二百，其後一匹為錢一千六百，輸一者過二，雖賦不增舊，而民愈困矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter as prices fell ever lower, what was paid grew ever greater: a bolt of silk equaled three thousand two hundred cash, later one bolt one thousand six hundred; what was paid as one became more than two. Though the nominal levy did not exceed the old amount, the people were ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Prices then kept falling while payments rose: a bolt of silk worth 3,200 cash, later only 1,600, yet taxpayers still owed more than double the original quota. The nominal rate never rose, but the burden doubled.

sentences.zh: 度支以稅物頒諸司，皆增本價為虛估給之，而繆以濫惡督州縣剝價，謂之折納。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Revenue distributed tax goods to the various offices, all inflating original prices in false valuation for disbursement, then wrongly pressing the prefectures and counties to cut prices on the pretext of shoddy goods—this was called "folded collection."
translations.idiomatic: The directorate distributed tax goods to ministries at inflated "book" valuations, then forced prefectures to accept shoddy goods at slashed prices—"folded collection."

sentences.zh: 復有「進奉」、「宣索」之名，改科役曰「召雇」，率配曰「和市」，以巧避微文，比大曆之數再倍。

translations.literal: There were again names such as "tribute presented" and "imperial requisition"; corvée levies were renamed "summoned hire," and proportional exactions called "harmonized purchase," artfully evading fine statutes until the total doubled the Dali figures.
translations.idiomatic: New labels appeared—"tribute presented," "imperial requisition"—while corvée became "summoned hire" and requisitions "harmonized purchase." Evasions of statute doubled Dali-era exactions.

sentences.zh: 又癘疫水旱，戶口減耗，刺史析戶，張虛數以寬責。

translations.literal: Again plague, flood, and drought reduced population; prefects split households and inflated numbers to ease their quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Plague, flood, and drought shrank the population; prefects split households and padded registers to meet quotas.

sentences.zh: 逃死闕稅，取於居者，一室空而四鄰亦盡。

translations.literal: Tax lost through flight and death was taken from those who remained; one house empty and all four neighbors were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes lost to flight and death were shifted onto those who stayed; one vacant house could ruin an entire neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 戶版不緝，無浮游之禁，州縣行小惠以傾誘鄰境，新收者優假之，唯安居不遷之民，賦役日重。

translations.literal: Household registers were not kept in order; there was no ban on vagrancy; prefectures and counties offered petty favors to lure people from neighboring districts; newcomers were indulged, while only those who stayed put without moving saw their levies grow daily heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Registers fell into disorder and vagrancy went unchecked. Counties lured neighbors' subjects with favors, easing taxes on newcomers while long-settled households paid ever more.

sentences.zh: 帝以問宰相陸贄，贄上疏請釐革其甚害者，大略有六：其一曰：

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the chief minister Lu Zhi; Zhi submitted a memorial requesting reform of the worst abuses, in six main points. The first said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked chief minister Lu Zhi for remedy. Zhi memorialized with six major reforms. The first point:

sentences.zh: :國家賦役之法，曰租、曰調、曰庸。

translations.literal: The state's levy and corvée law comprises zu, diao, and yong.
translations.idiomatic: The state's tax and corvée system comprises zu, diao, and yong.

sentences.zh: 其取法遠，其斂財均，其域人固。

translations.literal: Its method of collection was far-reaching, its gathering of wealth even, and its binding of the people firm.
translations.idiomatic: Its reach was broad, its burdens even, and its hold on the people secure.

sentences.zh: 有田則有租，有家則有調，有身則有庸，天下法制均壹，雖轉徙莫容其姦，故人無搖心。

translations.literal: Where there was field there was zu, where there was household there was diao, where there was person there was yong; the laws of the realm were uniform, and though people moved they could not evade fraud—thus the people had no unsettled minds.
translations.idiomatic: Land brought zu, households diao, persons yong. Law was uniform empire-wide; even migrants could not easily evade duty, so people felt secure in their obligations.

sentences.zh: 天寶之季，海內波蕩，版圖隳於避地，賦法壞於奉軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the realm was shaken; maps were lost through flight from territory; the tax law was ruined through supply to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao years the realm convulsed; maps were lost as people fled; tax law broke down under army supply demands.

sentences.zh: 賦役舊法，行之百年，人以為便。

translations.literal: The old levy and corvée law had been in force a hundred years, and people regarded it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The old system had run a century and people considered it workable.

sentences.zh: 兵興，供億不常，誅求隳制，此時弊，非法弊也。

translations.literal: When war arose, provisioning was inconstant and exactions destroyed the system—this was a defect of the times, not a defect of the law.
translations.idiomatic: War made supply irregular and exactions wrecked administration—that was a failure of the moment, not of the statute itself.

sentences.zh: 時有弊而未理，法無弊而已更。

translations.literal: There were defects of the time that were not remedied, while a law without defect was already changed.
translations.idiomatic: Timely abuses went unreformed while a sound law was discarded.

sentences.zh: 兩稅新制，竭耗編甿，日日滋甚。

translations.literal: The new two-tax system exhausted the registered peasantry, growing worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The new two-tax system drained the registered peasantry daily.

sentences.zh: 陛下初即位，宜損上益下，嗇用節財，而摘郡邑，驗簿書，州取大曆中一年科率多者為兩稅定法，此總無名之暴賦而立常規也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first took the throne, you should have reduced burdens above and benefited those below, economized expenditure and husbanded wealth; yet you picked through prefectures and counties, verified ledgers, and took the highest annual exaction rate of the Dali era in each province as the fixed two-tax law—this was to sum nameless violent levies and make them regular.
translations.idiomatic: On accession you should have eased burdens on the people; instead each province's highest Dali-era annual exaction became the fixed two-tax quota—turning arbitrary surcharges into permanent law.

sentences.zh: 夫財之所生，必因人力。

translations.literal: Wealth is produced only through human labor.
translations.idiomatic: All wealth comes from human labor.

sentences.zh: 兩稅以資產為宗，不以丁身為本，資產少者稅輕，多者稅重。

translations.literal: The two taxes take assets as their principle, not persons as their basis: those with few assets pay lightly, those with many pay heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The two taxes assess property, not persons: the poor pay little, the rich much.

sentences.zh: 不知有藏於襟懷囊篋，物貴而人莫窺者；

translations.literal: They do not know those who hide valuables in bosom, bag, and casket—goods costly yet unseen by others;
translations.idiomatic: They cannot see cash hoarded on one's person—wealth invisible to assessors;

sentences.zh: 有場圃、囷倉，直輕而衆以為富者；

translations.literal: those with farmyards and granaries, of low valuation yet regarded by the multitude as rich;
translations.idiomatic: farmyards and granaries valued cheaply yet deemed wealthy by neighbors;

sentences.zh: 有流通蕃息之貨，數寡而日收其贏者；

translations.literal: those with goods in circulation that multiply, few in number yet daily gathering profit;
translations.idiomatic: trading stock that turns over fast with small inventory but steady profit;

sentences.zh: 有廬舍器用，價高而終歲利寡者。

translations.literal: those with dwellings and utensils, high in price yet yielding little profit through the year.
translations.idiomatic: mansions and tools priced high yet yielding little annual return.

sentences.zh: 計估算緡，失平長偽，挾輕費轉徙者脫傜稅，敦本業者困斂求。

translations.literal: Calculating and assessing by strings of cash loses fairness and fosters fraud; those who hold light goods and move away escape corvée and tax, while those who devote themselves to basic occupations are trapped by collection.
translations.idiomatic: Cash-string assessments are unfair and invite fraud: those with portable wealth flee; those tied to farming bear the heaviest levies.

sentences.zh: 此誘之為姦，敺之避役也。

translations.literal: This tempts people to wrongdoing and drives them to evade service.
translations.idiomatic: The system rewards deceit and flight from duty.

sentences.zh: 今傜賦輕重相百，而以舊為準，重處流亡益多，輕處歸附益衆。

translations.literal: Today corvée and tax burdens differ by a hundredfold, yet the old standard is used as the basis; where burdens are heavy, flight increases; where light, settlement increases.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and tax burdens now vary a hundredfold, yet old quotas stand. Heavy districts lose population; light ones gain settlers.

sentences.zh: 有流亡則攤出，已重者愈重；

translations.literal: Where there is flight, assessments are spread outward, and what was already heavy grows heavier;
translations.idiomatic: Flight forces surcharges onto those who remain, worsening already heavy districts;

sentences.zh: 有歸附則散出，已輕者愈輕。

translations.literal: where there is settlement, assessments are dispersed, and what was already light grows lighter.
translations.idiomatic: settlement disperses quotas, easing already light districts.

sentences.zh: 人嬰其弊。

translations.literal: The people are caught in these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The people are crushed between the two.

sentences.zh: 願詔有司與宰相量年支，有不急者罷之，廣費者節之。

translations.literal: I wish that the relevant offices, with the chief ministers, measure annual expenditure; what is not urgent should be stopped, what is extravagant reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Let relevant offices and chief ministers tally annual needs, abolish non-urgent spending, and cut extravagance.

sentences.zh: 軍興加稅，諸道權宜所增，皆可停。

translations.literal: War levies and circuit emergency surcharges may all be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime surcharges and circuit emergency taxes should cease.

sentences.zh: 稅物估價，宜視月平，至京與色樣符者，不得虛稱折估。

translations.literal: Valuation of tax goods should follow the monthly fair price; what reaches the capital must match sample and quality, and false "folded valuation" must not be claimed.
translations.idiomatic: Tax goods should be valued at monthly fair prices; capital deliveries must match samples, without false "folded" discounts.

sentences.zh: 有濫惡，罪官吏，勿督百姓。

translations.literal: If goods are shoddy, punish the officials; do not press the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Punish officials for shoddy goods, not commoners.

sentences.zh: 每道以知兩稅判官一人與度支參計戶數，量土地沃瘠、物產多少為二等，州等下者配錢少，高者配錢多。

translations.literal: In each circuit let one official who knows the two taxes join the Directorate of Revenue in counting households, measuring land fertility and product abundance into two grades; lower-grade prefectures should be assigned less cash, higher-grade more.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit should assign one two-tax officer with the directorate to count households and rank land fertility and products; poorer prefectures owe less cash, richer ones more.

sentences.zh: 不變法而逋逃漸息矣。

translations.literal: Without changing the law, flight will gradually cease.
translations.idiomatic: Without changing the law itself, flight would gradually end.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second point says:
translations.idiomatic: The second point:

sentences.zh: :播殖非力不成，故先王定賦以布、麻、繒、纊、百穀，勉人功也。

translations.literal: Sowing and planting are not accomplished without labor; therefore the former kings fixed levies in cloth, hemp, silk, fine silk, and the hundred grains to encourage human effort.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture requires labor; ancient kings therefore levied cloth, hemp, silk, and grain to reward work.

sentences.zh: 又懼物失貴賤之平，交易難準，乃定貨泉以節輕重。

translations.literal: They also feared that goods would lose the balance of high and low value and that exchange would be hard to standardize, and so fixed currency to regulate weight in value.
translations.idiomatic: They also feared unstable prices and fixed currency to regulate value.

sentences.zh: 蓋為國之利權，守之在官，不以任下。

translations.literal: This was the state's profit and power, kept in the hands of officials and not entrusted to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Monetary profit and power belonged to the state, held by officials, not delegated downward.

sentences.zh: 然則穀帛，人所為也；

translations.literal: Thus grain and cloth are what people make;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and cloth are what people produce;

sentences.zh: 錢貨，官所為也。

translations.literal: cash is what the government makes.
translations.idiomatic: cash is what government mints.

sentences.zh: 人所為者，租稅取焉；

translations.literal: what people make is taken for zu and tax;
translations.idiomatic: What people make supplies zu and tax;

sentences.zh: 官所為者，賦斂捨焉。

translations.literal: what the government makes is set aside from levies.
translations.idiomatic: what government mints is kept out of direct levies.

sentences.zh: 國朝著令，租出穀，庸出絹，調出繒、纊、布、麻，曷嘗禁人鑄錢而以錢為賦？

translations.literal: Our dynasty's established orders had zu from grain, yong from silk, diao from silk, fine silk, cloth, and hemp—when did it ever forbid people from casting cash yet take cash as the levy?
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic law had zu from grain, yong from silk, diao from silk and cloth—when did the throne forbid private coinage yet demand cash as tax?

sentences.zh: 今兩稅効算緡之末法，估資產為差，以錢穀定稅，折供雜物，歲目頗殊。

translations.literal: Now the two taxes imitate the late law of assessing by strings of cash, estimate assets for gradation, fix tax in cash and grain, and convert payment into miscellaneous goods—the annual items differ greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The two taxes imitate late cash-string assessment, grade by property, fix dues in cash and grain, then convert to assorted goods—annual quotas wildly inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 所供非所業，所業非所供，增價以市所無，減價以貿所有，耕織之力有限，而物價貴錢無常。

translations.literal: What is supplied is not what is produced, what is produced is not what is supplied; prices are raised to buy what one lacks, lowered to trade what one has; the power of plowing and weaving is limited, while commodity prices and the value of cash have no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Taxpayers must deliver what they do not grow, at prices they cannot control, while farming and weaving capacity is finite and markets swing without warning.

sentences.zh: 初定兩稅，萬錢為絹三匹，價貴而數不多。

translations.literal: When the two taxes were first fixed, ten thousand cash equaled three bolts of silk—goods costly and the quantity not great.
translations.idiomatic: At first ten thousand cash equaled three bolts of silk—high prices, modest quantities.

sentences.zh: 及給軍裝，計數不計價，此稅少國用不充也。

translations.literal: When army equipment was supplied, quantity was counted, not price—thus the levy was small and state use insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Army issue counted bolts, not value—revenue fell short.

sentences.zh: 近者萬錢為絹六匹，價賤而數加。

translations.literal: Recently ten thousand cash equals six bolts of silk—goods cheap and the quantity increased.
translations.idiomatic: Recently ten thousand cash buys six bolts—cheap goods, doubled quantities.

sentences.zh: 計口蠶織不殊，而所輸倍，此供稅多人力不給也。

translations.literal: Per capita silkworm rearing and weaving are not different, yet what is paid is doubled—this is that supply and tax are great while human power cannot meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Households weave no more than before yet pay double—burdens outran labor.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司覆初定兩稅之歲絹、布定估，為布帛之數，復庸、調舊制，隨土所宜，各脩家技。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the relevant offices to review the fixed valuations of silk and cloth in the year when the two taxes were first set, establish the quantities in cloth, restore the old yong and diao systems, and according to what each region suits, let each repair his household craft.
translations.idiomatic: Offices should restore the original silk and cloth valuations from the first two-tax year, reinstate yong and diao, and let each household pursue its local craft as soil permits.

sentences.zh: 物甚賤，所出不加；

translations.literal: When goods are very cheap, what is paid out is not increased;
translations.idiomatic: When prices are very low, payments should not rise;

sentences.zh: 物甚貴，所入不減。

translations.literal: when goods are very costly, what is taken in is not reduced.
translations.idiomatic: when prices are very high, collections should not fall.

sentences.zh: 且經費所資，在錢者獨月俸、資課，以錢數多少給布，廣鑄而禁用銅器，則錢不乏。

translations.literal: Moreover, of expenditures supported, only monthly salaries and stipends require cash; according to the amount of cash, cloth should be issued; cast broadly and forbid copper vessels, and cash will not be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Routine spending needs cash only for salaries and stipends, which can be paid in cloth by cash value. Expand minting and ban private copperware, and money will suffice.

sentences.zh: 有糴鹽以入直，榷酒以納資，何慮無所給哉！

translations.literal: There is selling salt to obtain revenue and monopolizing wine to collect funds—why worry that there will be nothing to supply?
translations.idiomatic: Salt sales and wine monopolies can fund the state—why strip farmers?

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third point says:
translations.idiomatic: The third point:

sentences.zh: :廉使奏吏之能者有四科，一曰戶口增加，二曰田野墾闢，三曰稅錢長數，四曰率辦先期。

translations.literal: The ability of officials reported by inspection commissioners has four categories: first, increase in registered population; second, opening of fields; third, growth in tax cash; fourth, completing quotas ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors ranked officials on four counts: population growth, land reclaimed, tax revenue growth, and early quota completion.

sentences.zh: 夫貴戶口增加，詭情以誘姦浮，苛法以析親族，所誘者將議薄征則遽散，所析者不勝重稅而亡，有州縣破傷之病。

translations.literal: To prize population increase is to use deceit to lure the shiftless, harsh laws to split kindred; those lured disperse when lighter levies are discussed, those split cannot bear heavy tax and perish—there is the ailment of broken prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Praising population growth invites fraud and family-splitting to dodge tax; the lured flee when rates ease, the split cannot pay and die—counties are ruined.

sentences.zh: 貴田野墾闢，率民殖荒田，限年免租，新畝雖闢，舊畬蕪矣。

translations.literal: To prize opening of fields is to lead the people to plant waste land with rent exemption for a set term; though new mu are opened, old fallow land lies waste.
translations.idiomatic: Praising reclamation drives planting wasteland with rent holidays; new acres open while old fields lie fallow.

sentences.zh: 人以免租年滿，復為污萊，有稼穡不增之病。

translations.literal: When the rent-exemption term ends, people again make foul waste—there is the ailment that tillage does not increase.
translations.idiomatic: When exemptions expire, fields revert to waste—tillage never truly grows.

sentences.zh: 貴稅錢長數，重困疲羸，捶骨瀝髓，苟媚聚斂之司，有不恤人之病。

translations.literal: To prize growth in tax cash is to heavily afflict the weary and weak, beat the bone and drain the marrow, fawning on revenue offices—there is the ailment of not caring for people.
translations.idiomatic: Praising revenue growth crushes the weak and rewards extortionists—officials forget the people.

sentences.zh: 貴率辦先期，作威殘人，絲不容織，粟不暇舂，貧者奔迸，有不恕物之病。

translations.literal: To prize completing quotas ahead of schedule is to make power cruel to people, not allowing silk to be woven or grain threshed; the poor flee in panic—there is the ailment of not sparing goods.
translations.idiomatic: Praising early collection leaves no time to weave or thresh; the poor flee—production itself is harmed.

sentences.zh: 四病繇考覈不切事情之過。

translations.literal: The four ailments come from examination not matching real circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: All four ills stem from performance reviews divorced from reality.

sentences.zh: 驗之以實，則租賦所加，固有受其損者，此州若增客戶，彼郡必減居人。

translations.literal: Verified by fact, of what rent and tax is added there are certainly those who suffer loss; if this prefecture increases guest households, that commandery must reduce resident population.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, added tax burdens someone: one prefecture's "growth" is another's loss of residents.

sentences.zh: 增處邀賞而稅數加，減處懼罪而稅數不降。

translations.literal: Where there is increase, rewards are sought and tax numbers rise; where there is decrease, fear of guilt keeps tax numbers from falling.
translations.idiomatic: Growing districts chase rewards and raise quotas; shrinking ones fear punishment and never lower them.

sentences.zh: 國家設考課之法，非欲崇聚斂也。

translations.literal: The state established the examination law not to exalt revenue gathering.
translations.idiomatic: The examination system was never meant to glorify extraction.

sentences.zh: 宜命有司詳考課績，州稅有定，傜役有等，覆實然後報戶部。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the relevant offices to examine performance in detail; prefectural tax should be fixed, corvée graded, and only after review reported to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Offices should audit performance carefully, fix prefectural tax and corvée grades, and report to the Ministry of Revenue only after verification.

sentences.zh: 若人益阜實，稅額有餘，據戶均減十三為上課，減二次之，減一又次之。

translations.literal: If people grow more numerous and solid, and tax quota has surplus, reduce by three-tenths per household for top grade, by two-tenths for second, by one-tenth for third.
translations.idiomatic: Where population and wealth grow and quotas exceed need, cut assessments by thirty, twenty, or ten percent by grade.

sentences.zh: 若流亡多，加稅見戶者，殿亦如之。

translations.literal: If flight is great and tax is added to visible households, demotion should be applied likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Where flight is heavy and survivors are surcharged, officials should be demoted likewise.

sentences.zh: 民納租以去歲輸數為常，罷據額所率者。

translations.literal: The people should pay rent using last year's delivered amount as the norm, and stop collection according to quota targets.
translations.idiomatic: Payments should follow last year's actual delivery, not quota targets.

sentences.zh: 增闢勿益租，廢耕不降數。

translations.literal: Opening new land should not increase rent; abandoning tillage should not lower the count.
translations.idiomatic: Reclamation must not raise rent; abandoned fields must not reduce headcounts artificially.

sentences.zh: 定戶之際，視雜產以校之。

translations.literal: At the time of fixing households, miscellaneous production should be used for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Household registration should weigh miscellaneous production fairly.

sentences.zh: 田既有常租，則不宜復入兩稅。

translations.literal: Where fields already have regular rent, they should not again enter the two taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Land already paying regular rent should not be taxed again under the two-tax system.

sentences.zh: 如此，不督課而人人樂耕矣。

translations.literal: Thus, without pressing for revenue, every person would delight in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Then people would farm willingly without coercion.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：

translations.literal: The fourth point says:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth point:

sentences.zh: :明君不厚所資而害所養，故先人事而借其暇力，家給然後斂餘財。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler does not enrich what is taken and harm what is nurtured; therefore the former kings put human affairs first and borrowed spare labor, and only after households were provided for did they gather surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Wise rulers do not fund the state by starving the people. Ancient kings used labor in season and taxed only after households were secure.

sentences.zh: 今督收迫促，蠶事方興而輸縑，農功未艾而斂穀。

translations.literal: Now collection is pressed urgently: while silkworms are just active, silk is levied; while farming is not finished, grain is collected.
translations.idiomatic: Collection is rushed: silk is demanded at mulberry season, grain before harvest ends.

sentences.zh: 有者急賣而耗半直，無者求假費倍。

translations.literal: Those who have goods sell in haste and lose half their value; those who lack goods borrow at double cost.
translations.idiomatic: Owners sell cheap in panic; the poor borrow at usurious rates.

sentences.zh: 定兩稅之初，期約未詳，屬征役多故，率先限以收。

translations.literal: When the two taxes were first fixed, deadlines were not detailed; as corvée and levies multiplied, collection was rushed to meet early limits.
translations.idiomatic: Early two-tax rules lacked clear deadlines; wartime exactions forced premature collection.

sentences.zh: 宜定稅期，隨風俗時候，務於紓人。

translations.literal: Tax deadlines should be fixed according to local custom and season, with the aim of easing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Set tax seasons by local custom to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 其五曰：

translations.literal: The fifth point says:
translations.idiomatic: The fifth point:

sentences.zh: :頃師旅亟興，官司所儲，唯給軍食，凶荒不遑賑救。

translations.literal: Recently armies rose repeatedly; what offices stored supplied only army food, and amid famine there was no leisure for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Constant warfare left granaries for soldiers alone; famine relief was neglected.

sentences.zh: 人小乏則取息利，大乏則鬻田廬。

translations.literal: When people lacked a little, they took interest loans; when they lacked much, they sold fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: Minor want drove men to usury; utter ruin forced sale of land and home.

sentences.zh: 斂穫始畢，執契行貸，饑歲室家相棄，乞為奴僕，猶莫之售，或縊死道途。

translations.literal: When harvest was just finished, they held contracts and went to borrow; in famine years families abandoned one another, begging to be slaves yet finding no buyer, some hanging themselves on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh harvest brought loan sharks; in famine years families cast off kin, offered themselves as slaves unsold, and hanged themselves on the roads.

sentences.zh: 天災流行，四方代有。

translations.literal: Heavenly disasters spread, each region in turn suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters struck every region in turn.

sentences.zh: 稅茶錢積戶部者，宜計諸道戶口均之。

translations.literal: Tea tax money accumulated at the Ministry of Revenue should be divided equally by household registers in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tea-tax reserves at the Ministry of Revenue should be distributed by circuit population.

sentences.zh: 穀麥熟則平糴，亦以義倉為名，主以巡院。

translations.literal: When grain and wheat ripen, fair purchase should be made, also under the name of charity granary, administered by patrol offices.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest, the state should buy grain fairly through charity-granary offices under patrol commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時稔傷農，則優價廣糴，穀貴而止；

translations.literal: When the year is abundant and farming is hurt, buy at favorable price broadly and stop when grain is costly;
translations.idiomatic: In bumper years hurtful to farmers, buy generously at fair prices until prices rise;

sentences.zh: 小歉則借貸。

translations.literal: in slight shortage, lend.
translations.idiomatic: in lean years, lend.

sentences.zh: 循環斂散，使聚穀幸災者無以牟大利。

translations.literal: Circulating collection and release, so those who hoard grain to profit from disaster cannot gain great advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Rotate stockpiles so hoarders cannot profit from famine.

sentences.zh: 其六曰：

translations.literal: The sixth point says:
translations.idiomatic: The sixth point:

sentences.zh: :古者百畝地號一夫，蓋一夫授田不得過百畝，欲使人不廢業，田無曠耕。

translations.literal: In antiquity a hundred mu of land was called one husbandman; generally one husbandman was granted land not exceeding a hundred mu, wishing to make people not abandon their work and fields not lie idle.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity allotted one cultivator no more than a hundred mu so none would abandon farming or leave land idle.

sentences.zh: 今富者萬畝，貧者無容足之居，依託彊家，為其私屬，終歲服勞，常患不充。

translations.literal: Today the rich have ten thousand mu, the poor have no room for foot to stand; relying on powerful houses as private dependents, they labor all year yet often fear they cannot be filled.
translations.idiomatic: Today the rich hold ten thousand mu while the poor lack footing, attaching to great houses as dependents, laboring all year yet still hungry.

sentences.zh: 有田之家坐食租稅，京畿田畝稅五升，而私家收租畝一石，官取一，私取十，穡者安得足食？

translations.literal: Those with fields sit eating rent and tax; in the capital region field tax is five sheng per mu, yet private rent is one shi per mu—the government takes one, the private ten—how can the tiller get full food?
translations.idiomatic: Landlords live on rent: capital fields owed the state five sheng per mu but private landlords ten times that—one part to the throne, ten to the lord—how could peasants eat their fill?

sentences.zh: 宜為占田條限，裁租價，損有餘，優不足，此安富恤窮之善經，不可捨也。

translations.literal: There should be limits on occupied land, regulation of rent price, reduction for the surplus and favor for the insufficient—this is the excellent constant of securing the rich and relieving the poor and cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Set land ceilings, cap rents, tax the rich lightly and aid the poor—classic policy for social balance and not to be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 贄言雖切，以讒逐，事無施行者。

translations.literal: Though Zhi's words were earnest, he was driven out by slander and nothing was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's counsel was urgent, but slander drove him out and none of it was enacted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，河南尹齊抗復論其弊，以為：「軍興，國用稍廣，隨要而稅，吏擾人勞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Prefect of Henan Qi Kang again discussed its abuses, holding: "When war arose, state use grew somewhat broad; taxes followed need and clerks harassed the people with labor.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve, Henan prefect Qi Kang renewed the critique: war had widened spending, ad hoc taxes multiplied, and clerks tormented the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下變為兩稅，督納有時，貪暴無容其姦。

translations.literal: Your Majesty changed to the two taxes, with supervised payment on schedule, so greed and violence had no room for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's two-tax reform timed collection and checked official extortion.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，府庫充牣。

translations.literal: Within twenty years the treasuries were full.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty years the treasuries filled.

sentences.zh: 但定稅之初，錢輕貨重，故陛下以錢為稅。

translations.literal: But when tax was first fixed, cash was light and goods heavy, so Your Majesty took cash as the tax.
translations.idiomatic: At first cash was cheap and goods dear, so the throne taxed in money.

sentences.zh: 今錢重貨輕，若更為稅名，以就其輕，其利有六：吏絕其姦，一也；

translations.literal: Now cash is heavy and goods light; if the tax name were changed to follow the light value, the benefits would be six: clerks would lose their fraud, first;
translations.idiomatic: Now money is dear and goods cheap. Renaming the tax to follow commodity values would yield six gains: first, officials could not cheat;

sentences.zh: 人用不擾，二也；

translations.literal: the people's use would not be disturbed, second;
translations.idiomatic: second, the people would not be harassed;

sentences.zh: 靜而獲利，三也；

translations.literal: profit gained in stillness, third;
translations.idiomatic: third, revenue would rise without turmoil;

sentences.zh: 用不乏錢，四也；

translations.literal: use would not lack cash, fourth;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the treasury would not lack coin;

sentences.zh: 不勞而易知，五也；

translations.literal: without labor yet easy to know, fifth;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, rules would be simple;

sentences.zh: 農桑自勸，六也。

translations.literal: farming and sericulture would encourage themselves, sixth.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, farming and sericulture would revive themselves.

sentences.zh: 百姓本出布帛，而稅反配錢，至輸時復取布帛，更為三估計折，州縣升降成姦。

translations.literal: The common people fundamentally produce cloth and silk, yet tax is assigned in cash; at delivery time cloth and silk are again taken, further subjected to triple valuation and folding, and prefectures and counties raise or lower to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers produce cloth and silk, yet taxes are assessed in cash and collected in cloth after triple valuation—prefectures manipulate prices at will.

sentences.zh: 若直定布帛，無估可折。

translations.literal: If cloth and silk were fixed directly, there would be no valuation to fold.
translations.idiomatic: Fix payment in cloth and silk and valuation fraud ends.

sentences.zh: 蓋以錢為稅，則人力竭而有司不之覺。

translations.literal: Generally, taking cash as tax, human power is exhausted yet the offices do not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Cash taxation exhausts labor while officials remain blind to it.

sentences.zh: 今兩稅出於農人，農人所有，唯布帛而已。

translations.literal: Now the two taxes come from farmers; what farmers possess is only cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The two taxes fall on farmers, who own only cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 用布帛處多，用錢處少，又有鼓鑄以助國計，何必取於農人哉？

translations.literal: Where cloth and silk are used is many, where cash is used few; moreover casting assists state accounts—why must it be taken from farmers?
translations.idiomatic: Cloth and silk circulate widely; coin is needed less, and minting aids the treasury—why burden farmers?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，亦不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered and again received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in and again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗居奉天，儲畜空窘，嘗遣卒視賊，以苦寒乞襦絝，帝不能致，剔親王帶金而鬻之。

translations.literal: At first, when Dezong dwelt at Fengtian, stores were empty and straitened; he once sent soldiers to observe the rebels, who begged for padded coats in bitter cold; the emperor could not provide them and stripped gold from princes' belts to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's refuge at Fengtian, stores were bare. Soldiers scouting rebels begged for winter coats the emperor could not supply; he sold princes' belt gold instead.

sentences.zh: 朱泚既平，於是帝屬意聚斂，常賦之外，進奉不息。

translations.literal: After Zhu Ci was pacified, the emperor then set his mind on accumulation; beyond regular levies, tribute presented did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's defeat, Dezong turned to hoarding; beyond regular taxes, "presented tribute" never stopped.

sentences.zh: 劍南西川節度使韋皋有「日進」，江西觀察使李兼有「月進」，淮南節度使杜亞、宣歙觀察使劉贊、鎮海節度使王緯李錡皆徼射恩澤，以常賦入貢，名為「羨餘」。

translations.literal: The military governor of Jiannan West Wei Gao had "daily presentation," the observation commissioner of Jiangxi Li Jian had "monthly presentation"; the military governors Du Ya of Huainan, Liu Zan of Xuan-She, Wang Wei and Li Qian of Zhenhai all angled for favor, entering regular levies as tribute under the name "surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao in Jiannan sent "daily tribute," Li Jian in Jiangxi "monthly tribute"; Du Ya, Liu Zan, Wang Wei, and Li Qian converted regular taxes into "surplus" gifts for favor.

sentences.zh: 至代易又有「進奉」。

translations.literal: When successors took office there was again "presented tribute."
translations.idiomatic: Each new appointee brought fresh "presented tribute."

sentences.zh: 當是時，戶部錢物，所在州府及巡院皆得擅留，或矯密旨加斂，謫官吏、刻祿稟，增稅通津、死人及蔬果。

translations.literal: At this time Ministry of Revenue funds and goods in every prefecture and patrol office could be retained at will, or secret edicts forged for added levies, officials demoted, salaries and rations cut, taxes increased at ferries, on the dead, and on fruits and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue offices everywhere hoarded funds, forged secret edicts for surcharges, cut salaries, and taxed ferries, corpses, even fruit and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 凡代易進奉，取於稅入，十獻二三，無敢問者。

translations.literal: Whenever successors presented tribute, it was taken from tax intake, two or three parts in ten presented, and none dared inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Succession tributes skimmed two or three tenths of tax intake, and none dared object.

sentences.zh: 常州刺史裴肅鬻薪炭案紙為進奉，得遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: The prefect of Changzhou Pei Su sold firewood, charcoal, and desk paper as presented tribute and was promoted to Zhedong observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Pei Su sold firewood and paper as tribute and won promotion to Zhedong observer.

sentences.zh: 刺史進奉，自肅始也。

translations.literal: Prefects presenting tribute began with Su.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural tribute began with Pei Su.

sentences.zh: 劉贊卒于宣州，其判官嚴綬傾軍府為進奉，召為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Liu Zan died at Xuanzhou, his aide Yan Shou drained the military headquarters for presented tribute and was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan died, aide Yan Shou emptied the commandery treasury for tribute and became vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 判官進奉，自綬始也。

translations.literal: Aides presenting tribute began with Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Staff-level tribute began with Yan Shou.

sentences.zh: 自裴延齡用事，益為天子積私財，而生民重困。

translations.literal: From the time Pei Yanling held power, he further amassed private wealth for the Son of Heaven, and the living people were heavily afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Pei Yanling the emperor's private hoard grew and the people suffered doubly.

sentences.zh: 延齡死，而人相賀。

translations.literal: When Yanling died, people congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling died, people celebrated.

sentences.zh: 是時，宮中取物於市，以中官為宮市使。

translations.literal: At this time the palace took goods from the market, with eunuchs as palace-market commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The palace then bought through eunuch "palace market" agents.

sentences.zh: 兩市置「白望」數十百人，以鹽估敝衣、絹帛，尺寸分裂酬其直。

translations.literal: In the two markets several tens or hundreds of "white watchers" were placed, using salt to estimate worn clothing and silk, splitting inch by inch to pay their price.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of "white watchers" in the two markets priced goods with salt as a standard, paying threadbare cloth and silk penny by penny.

sentences.zh: 又索進奉門戶及脚價錢，有齎物入市而空歸者。

translations.literal: They also demanded presented-tribute household fees and porterage money; some who brought goods to market returned empty.
translations.idiomatic: They also extorted tribute fees and porterage; merchants sometimes returned with nothing.

sentences.zh: 每中官出，沽漿賣餅之家皆徹肆塞門。

translations.literal: Whenever eunuchs went out, shops selling gruel and cakes all shut and blocked their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever eunuchs appeared, noodle and cake shops shut their doors.

sentences.zh: 諫官御史數上疏諫，不聽，人不堪其弊。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and censors repeatedly submitted memorials of advice, but the emperor would not listen; people could not bear the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Censors protested repeatedly, but the emperor ignored them; the abuse was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎蘇弁言：「京師游手數千萬家，無生業者仰宮市以活，奈何罷？

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of Revenue Su Bian said: "In the capital there are tens of millions of households of idlers; those without livelihood rely on the palace market to live—how can it be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Su Bian argued: millions in the capital lived off the palace market—how could it close?

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，以為然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹韋湊奏：「小人因宮市為姦，真偽難辨，宜下府縣供送。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Jingzhao Wei Cou memorialized: "Petty men use the palace market for fraud, true and false hard to distinguish; it is fitting to have prefectures and counties supply and deliver.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou, prefect of Jingzhao, proposed county supply instead because palace-market fraud was rampant.

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 中官言百姓賴宮市以養者也，湊反得罪。

translations.literal: Eunuchs said the common people relied on the palace market for sustenance, and Cou was punished in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs claimed the people needed the palace market; Cou was punished instead.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，乃罷宮市使及鹽鐵使月進。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, the palace-market commissioner and the salt-iron envoy's monthly presentation were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong abolished the palace market and monthly salt-iron tribute.

sentences.zh: 憲宗又罷除官受代進奉及諸道兩稅外榷率；

translations.literal: Xianzong again abolished incoming officials' succession tribute and extralegal monopolies beyond the two taxes in each circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ended succession tribute and circuit monopolies beyond the two taxes;

sentences.zh: 分天下之賦以為三，一曰上供，二曰送使，三曰留州。

translations.literal: the realm's levies were divided into three: first, tribute to the center; second, funds for envoys; third, retention by the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and split revenues into three shares: central tribute, envoy funds, and local retention.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴垍又令諸道節度、觀察調費取於所治州，不足則取於屬州，而屬州送使之餘與其上供者，皆輸度支。

translations.literal: The chief minister Pei Ji also ordered military governors and observation commissioners to adjust expenses from prefectures they governed, and if insufficient from subordinate prefectures; what subordinate prefectures had left after envoy funds and what they sent upward were all delivered to the Directorate of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji required governors to fund expenses from governed prefectures, then subordinates; surpluses went to the directorate of revenue.

sentences.zh: 是時，因德宗府庫之積，頗約費用，天子身服澣濯。

translations.literal: At this time, relying on Dezong's treasury accumulations, expenditures were somewhat reduced, and the Son of Heaven himself wore washed clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Dezong's hoard, Xianzong cut spending and wore patched robes.

sentences.zh: 及劉闢、李錡既平，訾藏皆入內庫。

translations.literal: After Liu Pi and Li Qian were pacified, stored wealth all entered the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After suppressing Liu Pi and Li Qian, seized wealth filled the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使于頔、河東節度使王鍔進獻甚厚，翰林學士李絳嘗諫曰：「方鎮進獻，因緣為姦，以侵百姓，非聖政所宜。

translations.literal: The military governor of Shannan East Dao Yu Di and the military governor of Hedong Wang E presented gifts very generously; the Hanlin academician Li Jiang once remonstrated: "Military governors' presentations become opportunities for fraud to encroach on the common people—not what sage government should do.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di and Wang E sent lavish gifts. Li Jiang warned: frontier gifts invite fraud and hurt the people—unworthy of sage rule.

sentences.zh: 」帝喟然曰：「誠知非至德事，然兩河中夏貢賦之地，朝覲久廢，河、湟陷沒，烽候列於郊甸。

translations.literal: " The emperor sighed and said: "I truly know this is not the utmost virtuous affair, yet the two rivers and central plain are tribute lands; court audiences long suspended, the He and Huang regions lost, beacon fires lined the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: he knew it was wrong, yet the heartland had long ceased tribute audiences, the northwest was lost, and beacons burned at the capital's edge.

sentences.zh: 方刷祖宗之恥，不忍重斂於人也。

translations.literal: We are wiping away the ancestors' shame and cannot bear to levy heavily on the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was redeeming ancestral shame and could not bear to tax the people further—so he said.

sentences.zh: 」然獨不知進獻之取於人者重矣。

translations.literal: " Yet alone he did not know that what presentations took from the people was heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he failed to see that presentations weighed heavier still on the people.

sentences.zh: 及討淮西，判度支楊於陵坐饋餫不繼貶，以司農卿皇甫鎛代之，由是益為刻剝。

translations.literal: When the Huai-Xi campaign began, Yang Yuling, acting director of revenue, was demoted for failure to keep supplies flowing; the Minister of Agriculture Huangfu Bo replaced him, and from this extraction grew harsher.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Huai-Xi, Yang Yuling was demoted for supply failures; Huangfu Bo replaced him and extraction grew crueler.

sentences.zh: 司農卿王遂、京兆尹李翛號能聚斂，乃以為宣歙、浙西觀察使，予之富饒之地，以辦財賦。

translations.literal: The Minister of Agriculture Wang Sui and the Prefect of Jingzhao Li Chong were famed for gathering wealth and were made observation commissioners of Xuan-She and Zhexi, given rich territories to handle fiscal levies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui and Li Chong, famed extortionists, were sent to rich Xuan-She and Zhexi to raise revenue.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使王播言：「劉晏領使時，自按租庸，然後知州縣錢穀利病虛實。

translations.literal: The salt-iron commissioner Wang Bo said: "When Liu Yan headed the commission, he himself examined zu and yong, and only then knew the profit, harm, emptiness, and fullness of prefectural cash and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo said Liu Yan had audited zu and yong himself to learn each prefecture's true fiscal condition.

sentences.zh: 」乃以副使程异巡江、淮，覈州府上供錢穀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the vice commissioner Cheng Yi toured the Jiang and Huai, auditing prefectural tribute cash and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent vice commissioner Cheng Yi to tour Jiang-Huai and audit tribute funds.

sentences.zh: 异至江、淮，得錢百八十五萬貫。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the Jiang and Huai, he obtained 1,850,000 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yi recovered 1.85 million strings from Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 其年，遂代播為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: That year he replaced Bo as salt-iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yi replaced Wang Bo as salt-iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北兵討王承宗，於是募人入粟河北、淮西者，自千斛以上皆授以官。

translations.literal: At this time the Hebei army campaigned against Wang Chengzong; thereupon those who contributed grain to Hebei and Huai-Xi were recruited, and from one thousand bushels upward all were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: While Hebei forces fought Wang Chengzong, the court recruited grain donors of a thousand bushels or more to Hebei and Huai-Xi with official posts.

sentences.zh: 度支鹽鐵與諸道貢獻尤甚，號「助軍錢」。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Revenue and salt-iron and the circuits' presentations were especially heavy, called "aid-the-army funds."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue, salt-iron, and circuit gifts surged under the name "aid-the-army funds."

sentences.zh: 及賊平，則有賀禮及助賞設物。

translations.literal: When rebels were pacified, there were congratulatory gifts and aid-reward provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After victories came congratulatory gifts and victory banquets.

sentences.zh: 羣臣上尊號，又有獻賀物。

translations.literal: When the ministers offered a honorific title, there were again congratulatory gifts presented.
translations.idiomatic: Honorific ceremonies brought further congratulatory gifts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，一切罷之，兩稅外加率一錢者，以枉法贓論。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, all were abolished; an extra levy of one cash beyond the two taxes was punished as corrupt-gains crime.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong abolished these exactions; adding even one cash above the two taxes was treated as corruption.

sentences.zh: 然自在藩邸時，習見用兵之弊，以謂戎臣武卒，法當姑息。

translations.literal: Yet while in the princely residence he had grown accustomed to the abuses of using troops, holding that military men and soldiers should by law be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as heir he had learned to indulge generals and soldiers as a matter of policy.

sentences.zh: 及即位，自神策諸軍，非時賞賜，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, from the Shence armies onward, untimely rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he showered the Shence armies with unscheduled rewards beyond count.

sentences.zh: 已而幽州兵囚張弘靖，鎮州殺田弘正，兩鎮用兵，置南北供軍院。

translations.literal: Soon after, Youzhou troops imprisoned Zhang Hongjing and Zhenzhou killed Tian Hongzheng; the two circuits went to war, and northern and southern army-supply offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou imprisoned Zhang Hongjing and Zhenzhou killed Tian Hongzheng; war between the two circuits followed, with north and south supply offices created.

sentences.zh: 而行營軍十五萬，不能亢兩鎮萬餘之眾。

translations.literal: Yet the field army of one hundred fifty thousand could not match the ten thousand-odd troops of the two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a field army of 150,000 could not overcome the two circuits' ten thousand-odd troops.

sentences.zh: 而饋運不能給，帛粟未至而諸軍或彊奪於道。

translations.literal: Transport could not supply them; before cloth and grain arrived the various armies sometimes seized by force on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Supply lines failed; armies seized grain and cloth on the roads before official deliveries arrived.

sentences.zh: 蓋自建中定兩稅，而物輕錢重，民以為患，至是四十年。

translations.literal: Generally, from the Jianzhong fixing of the two taxes, goods were light and cash heavy, and the people regarded it as a affliction—by this time forty years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jianzhong fixed the two taxes, commodities had been cheap and cash dear—a forty-year affliction for the people.

sentences.zh: 當時為絹二匹半者為八匹，大率加三倍。

translations.literal: What then was two and a half bolts of silk became eight bolts; on the whole it increased threefold.
translations.idiomatic: Silk dues that had been two and a half bolts became eight—roughly tripled.

sentences.zh: 豪家大商，積錢以逐輕重，故農人日困，末業日增。

translations.literal: Great houses and great merchants hoarded cash to chase light and heavy value, so farmers daily grew distressed and secondary trades daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Great merchants hoarded coin to play on price swings; farmers grew poorer while commerce expanded.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以貨輕錢重，民困而用不充，詔百官議革其弊。

translations.literal: The emperor also, because goods were light and cash heavy and the people distressed while use was insufficient, ordered the hundred officials to discuss reform of the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing goods cheap, cash dear, and revenue short, the emperor ordered officials to debate remedies.

sentences.zh: 而議者多請重挾銅之律。

translations.literal: But most debaters requested strengthening the law against hoarding copper.
translations.idiomatic: Most urged harsher anti-hoarding laws on copper.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書楊於陵曰：「王者制錢以權百貨，貿遷有無，通變不倦，使物無甚貴甚賤，其術非它，在上而已。

translations.literal: The Minister of Revenue Yang Yuling said: "The king fashions cash to balance the hundred goods, to move what exists and what lacks, changing without weariness, making goods neither very costly nor very cheap—the method is nothing else but what is above.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue minister Yang Yuling said: "The throne regulates currency to balance trade and keep prices stable—the key lies with the sovereign alone.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 上之所重，人必從之。

translations.literal: What the above values, people surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: What the court values, people follow.

sentences.zh: 古者權之於上，今索之於下；

translations.literal: In antiquity power lay above, today it is demanded from below;
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity kept monetary power above; today it is squeezed from below;

sentences.zh: 昔散之四方，今藏之公府；

translations.literal: formerly dispersed to the four quarters, today stored in the public treasury;
translations.idiomatic: once coin circulated widely; now it is locked in public vaults;

sentences.zh: 昔廣鑄以資用，今減鑪以廢功；

translations.literal: formerly casting broadly to supply use, today reducing furnaces to waste effort;
translations.idiomatic: minting was expanded for use; now furnaces are cut and production idled;

sentences.zh: 昔行之於中原，今洩之於邊裔。

translations.literal: formerly practiced in the central plain, today leaking to the border regions.
translations.idiomatic: once currency served the heartland; now it drains to the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 又有閭井送終之唅，商賈貸舉之積，江湖壓覆之耗，則錢焉得不重，貨焉得不輕？

translations.literal: There are also village burial ornaments, merchants' loan accumulations, and losses from rivers and lakes pressing and covering—how can cash not be heavy and goods not light?
translations.idiomatic: Village funeral hoards, merchant loans, and losses in transit further drain coin—no wonder cash is dear and goods cheap.

sentences.zh: 開元中，天下鑄錢七十餘鑪，歲盈百萬，今纔十數鑪，歲入十五萬而已。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, the realm had more than seventy mints, with yearly surplus of a million; now there are barely ten-odd mints, yearly intake only one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan had seventy mints yielding a million a year; now barely ten mints yield 150,000.

sentences.zh: 大曆以前，淄青、太原、魏博雜鉛鐵以通時用，嶺南雜以金、銀、丹砂、象齒，今一用泉貨，故錢不足。

translations.literal: Before the Dali era, Ziqing, Taiyuan, and Weibo mixed lead and iron for timely use; Lingnan mixed gold, silver, cinnabar, and ivory; now all use official coin, so cash is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Once rebellious circuits coined base metal and the south used gold and silver; now only official coin circulates, so money is scarce.

sentences.zh: 今宜使天下兩稅、榷酒、鹽利、上供及留州、送使錢，悉輸以布帛穀粟，則人寬於所求，然後出內府之積，收市廛之滯，廣山鑄之數，限邊裔之出，禁私家之積，則貨日重而錢日輕矣。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to have throughout the realm two taxes, wine monopoly, salt profits, tribute to the center, and retained and envoy funds all paid in cloth, silk, and grain; then the people will be eased in what is sought; thereafter bring out inner-treasury stores, buy up market stagnation, broaden mountain minting, limit border outflow, forbid private hoarding—then goods will daily grow heavy and cash daily light.
translations.idiomatic: Pay two taxes, monopolies, tribute, and retention in cloth and grain; then release imperial stores, buy up market surpluses, expand minting, limit border outflow, and ban private hoarding—commodities will rise and coin will cheapen.

sentences.zh: 」宰相善其議。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers approved.

sentences.zh: 由是兩稅、上供、留州，皆易以布帛、絲纊，租、庸、課、調不計錢而納布帛，唯鹽酒本以榷率計錢，與兩稅異，不可去錢。

translations.literal: Thereupon two taxes, tribute to the center, and retention were all exchanged for cloth, silk, and fine silk; zu, yong, duties, and diao did not count cash but paid cloth and silk; only salt and wine, being monopolies reckoned in cash, differed from the two taxes and could not abandon cash.
translations.idiomatic: Two taxes and tribute shifted to cloth and silk; zu, yong, and diao were paid in kind. Only salt and wine monopolies still used cash.

sentences.zh: 文宗大和九年，以天下回殘錢置常平義倉本錢，歲增市之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe of Wenzong, remnant cash throughout the realm was placed as capital for ever-normal and charity granaries, increased yearly by purchase.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenzong Dahe 9, remnant coin was assigned as ever-normal and charity granary capital, replenished by annual purchases.

sentences.zh: 非遇水旱不增者，判官罰俸，書下考；

translations.literal: If not encountering flood or drought and not increased, the judging official was fined salary and given low evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Officials who failed to increase reserves except in flood or drought lost salary and received poor evaluations;

sentences.zh: 州縣假借，以枉法論。

translations.literal: if prefectures and counties borrowed the funds, it was prosecuted as perversion of law.
translations.idiomatic: prefectural borrowing was prosecuted as corruption.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗召監倉御史崔虞問太倉粟數，對曰：「有粟二百五十萬石。

translations.literal: Wenzong once summoned the supervising censor of the granary Cui Yu to ask the Great Granary grain count; he replied: "There are 2,500,000 shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong asked supervising granary censor Cui Yu how much grain the Great Granary held; he answered 2.5 million shi.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今歲費廣而所畜寡，奈何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This year's expenses are broad yet stores few—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Expenses are high and stores low—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 」乃詔出使郎官、御史督察州縣壅遏錢穀者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict ordered dispatched court gentlemen and censors to inspect prefectures and counties that obstructed or hoarded cash and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered envoys and censors to investigate counties hoarding grain and funds.

sentences.zh: 時豪民侵噬產業不移戶，州縣不敢傜役，而征稅皆出下貧。

translations.literal: At this time powerful families encroached on estates without transferring household registration; prefectures and counties dared not impose corvée, and tax collection all came from the lowest poor.
translations.idiomatic: Great families swallowed estates without registering them; counties dared not conscript the powerful, taxing only the poorest.

sentences.zh: 至於依富室為奴客，役罰峻於州縣。

translations.literal: As for relying on rich houses as slave retainers, labor and penalties were harsher than from prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dependents of rich houses faced harsher labor and penalties than from the state.

sentences.zh: 長吏歲輒遣吏巡覆田稅，民苦其擾。

translations.literal: Senior officials yearly sent clerks to tour and review field tax; the people suffered from the harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Each year magistrates sent clerks to re-audit field tax, harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，廢浮圖法，天下毀寺四千六百、招提蘭若四萬，籍僧尼為民二十六萬五千人，奴婢十五萬人，田數千萬頃，大秦穆護、祅二千餘人。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, the Buddhist law was abolished; throughout the realm 4,600 monasteries were destroyed and 40,000 subsidiary shrines and hermitages, registering monks and nuns as common people 265,000, slaves and maids 150,000, fields several tens of millions of mu, and over 2,000 Manichean priests and Zoroastrians.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong suppressed Buddhism: 4,600 monasteries and 40,000 shrines destroyed, 265,000 clergy and 150,000 dependents secularized, millions of mu seized, and over 2,000 Manichean and Zoroastrian priests expelled.

sentences.zh: 上都、東都每街留寺二，每寺僧三十人，諸道留僧以三等，不過二十人。

translations.literal: In the upper and eastern capitals two monasteries per ward were kept, thirty monks per monastery; circuits retained monks by three grades, not exceeding twenty.
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals kept two temples per ward with thirty monks each; circuits kept up to twenty by grade.

sentences.zh: 腴田鬻錢送戶部，中下田給寺家奴婢丁壯者為兩稅戶，人十畝。

translations.literal: Fertile fields were sold for cash sent to the Ministry of Revenue; middle and lower fields were given to monastery slaves and maids, strong adult males made two-tax households at ten mu per person.
translations.idiomatic: Fertile monastic land was sold for revenue; lesser land went to former dependents registered as taxpayers at ten mu each.

sentences.zh: 以僧尼既盡，兩京悲田養病坊，給寺田十頃，諸州七頃，主以耆壽。

translations.literal: Since monks and nuns were gone, the two capitals' charity wards for the sick were given ten qing of monastic land each, seven qing in other prefectures, administered by elders.
translations.idiomatic: With clergy gone, charity hospitals in the capitals received ten qing of former temple land, seven in the provinces, run by elders.

sentences.zh: 自會昌末，置備邊庫，收度支、戶部、鹽鐵錢物。

translations.literal: From late Huichang, a frontier-reserve treasury was established, receiving funds and goods from the Directorate of Revenue, Ministry of Revenue, and salt-iron.
translations.idiomatic: From late Huichang a frontier reserve treasury absorbed revenue, salt-iron, and ministry funds.

sentences.zh: 宣宗更號延資庫。

translations.literal: Xuanzong renamed it the Extended-Funds Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong renamed it the Extended-Funds Treasury.

sentences.zh: 初以度支郎中判之，至是以屬宰相，其任益重。

translations.literal: At first a directorate-of-revenue bureau director judged it; from this time it was placed under the chief minister and its responsibility grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Initially a revenue bureau director managed it; later it fell under the chief minister with greater weight.

sentences.zh: 戶部歲送錢帛二十萬，度支鹽鐵送者三十萬，諸道進奉助軍錢皆輸焉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue yearly sent 200,000 in cash and cloth, the directorate of revenue and salt-iron 300,000, and circuits' presented aid-the-army funds were all delivered there.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue sent 200,000 yearly, revenue and salt-iron 300,000, and circuit aid-the-army gifts—all to this treasury.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，雲南蠻數內寇，徙兵戍嶺南。

translations.literal: In the time of Yizong, Yunnan barbarians repeatedly raided inward and troops were shifted to garrison Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yizong, Nanzhao raids drove troops south to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 淮北大水，征賦不能辦，人人思亂。

translations.literal: Great flood on the Huai north; levies could not be met and every person thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibei flooding prevented tax collection; rebellion was on every mind.

sentences.zh: 及龐勛反，附者六七萬。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, those who joined him numbered sixty or seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun's rebellion drew sixty or seventy thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 自關東至海大旱，冬蔬皆盡，貧者以蓬子為麵，槐葉為齏。

translations.literal: From Guandong to the sea great drought; winter vegetables were all gone, the poor taking cogon seed for flour and pagoda leaves for relish.
translations.idiomatic: Drought from Guandong to the coast destroyed winter crops; the poor ate cogon-root flour and pagoda-leaf relish.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，大水，山東饑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, great flood; Shandong suffered famine.
